Your AI can rebuild each tool on your site and show which ones ChatGPT can now match.

Since 7 October, ChatGPT answers can arrive as side-by-side comparisons and small tools built on request. OpenAI's own launch example was a savings calculator.

Our view is that a generic calculator or comparison table is no longer a defensible traffic asset. Rebuild those tools around what ChatGPT can't make up. Live prices, stock, a customer's own account data, a quote you'll honour.

Start with an audit. Give your AI a list of every calculator, quiz, guide and comparison table on your site, with traffic and leads from your analytics. It builds its own version of each and hands back a table of which it can match and which depend on something only you have.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/chatgpt-gpt-6-intelligent-ui-marketing-teams/
clips.text: When ChatGPT puts three products in columns, it fills each cell with whatever it found about price, specs and delivery. If your facts are scattered across PDFs, images and product pages that don't match, you risk a blank or wrong cell next to a competitor whose numbers were easy to read. But OpenAI hasn't said what data the comparisons draw on, so that's our inference from how ChatGPT search already works. So our view at Manual Focus is that a generic calculator or comparison table is no longer a defensible traffic asset. Rebuild those tools around what ChatGPT can't make up. Live prices, stock, a customer's own account data, a quote you'll honour.

Your AI can rebuild each tool on your site and show which ones ChatGPT can now match.

GPT-6 in ChatGPT can build a working calculator from a one-line request and lay products out in columns. That puts every simple tool on your website up against one a buyer can make in the chat.

Give your AI a list of your calculators, quizzes, guides and comparison tables, with sessions and leads. It builds its own version of each and tells you which of yours depend on something only you have, like live prices or account data.

Then give it your product page URLs. It checks whether price, key specs, dimensions and delivery terms are in plain text and drafts a consistent fact block for each product.

The prompts are in the show notes.

clips.text: Get AI on your interactive tools. Give it a list of every calculator, quiz, guide and comparison table on your site, with the traffic and leads from your analytics export. It builds its own version of each one and hands back a table: which of yours it can match, and which depend on something only you have, like live prices or account data. What you add after that is your team's call. Second. Get your AI on your product pages. Give it the URLs and it checks whether price, key specs, dimensions and delivery terms are readable in plain text, in the same format on every page, or buried in images and downloads. It flags the gaps and drafts a consistent fact block for each product.
